title: The World's Oldest Noodles Are 4,000 Years Old — and They're Chinese | China Travel Expert
description:
Forget the Marco Polo myth. The oldest bowl of noodles ever found is 4,000 years old — and it was dug up in China.

In 2005, archaeologists at the Lajia site in Qinghai Province found a sealed, overturned earthenware bowl under about three metres of sediment, left behind when the settlement was buried by disaster. Inside were long, thin, well-preserved noodles — made not from wheat but from two kinds of millet native to China. The find, published in the journal Nature, is the earliest empirical evidence of noodles anywhere on Earth. So the next time someone argues about who invented the noodle, you know where to point.

🧭 Expert Tip: To see China's living noodle craft, order hand-pulled lamian (拉面) — a good chef stretches a single lump of dough into hundreds of strands right in front of you.
